biggestProblem: The zero of the scale is real but the top of the scale is not, and the achievable-without-deserving floor sits ABOVE our shipped reading. A featureless smooth silhouette - no stem, no calyx notch, no sepals, C-infinity, convex or near-convex - scores referent_gain +0.434 at the SUITE frame's own mask_px 12600, found in 120 random draws of a 7-parameter superellipse/egg family. The shipped fruit on that same frame scores +0.300. The null the probe PRINTS beside it (ellipse_1.35) reads +0.026, understating the smooth-shape ceiling by 16x, because 1.35 happens to be near a local minimum of the aspect-ratio sweep. Any reading in the 0.3-0.45 band therefore carries no evidence that fruit-like relief is present, and 0.300 is inside that band.

evidence.what_the_probe_does_get_right: A rasterised circle scores +0.004 to +0.011 at every mask size tested and the SUITE frame's printed circle control is +0.0055 - unlike `identity`, which handed a provably convex sphere 1.000. The ordering circle < ellipse < tuned smooth blob < real trace is real and monotone. The min(limb_gain, sig_gain) rule does defeat the obvious attack: circle + k=40 ripple, circle + white radial noise and circle + spikes all stay <= 0.089 because sig_gain stays near zero. The mask is geometric, the scale matching is by construction, and the Lanczos test passes.

whatWouldGameIt: Optimising `referent_gain` does NOT drive an agent toward a stem, a calyx notch or sepals. It drives them toward a tuned smooth body. Concretely: (1) reshape any fruit as a superellipse with exponent ~1.6-2.0, aspect 1.0-1.5 and a 10-25% first-harmonic egg asymmetry plus one k=2/k=3 bump of 3-12% - a five-to-seven-number lathe profile with no appendage of any kind - and the number goes from 0.300 to 0.43-0.57 at every mask size from 2000 to 30000 px. (2) Read REFERENT_POLYS out of probes.py (it is in the repo, every agent can see it), low-pass one polygon to 8 harmonics and build that lathe profile: +0.75 to +0.92, inside the band the report reserves for real fruit, with zero stem and zero sepals. (3) Cheaper still, quote the wrong field: limb_gain reads 0.444 where the headline is 0.300, the in-file docs tell you limb_gain IS the headline, and limb_gain is bought by per-pixel rim raggedness. (4) Choose the frame: at mask ~2000-2200 an ellipse of aspect 1.20 alone reads +0.413, so a portrait shot of a small fruit produces a flattering number with no geometry change at all. What it CANNOT be gamed by, tested: smoothing our current silhouette (k<=8 low-pass of the shipped mask gives +0.260, below the delivered +0.300), decorating a circle with ripple/noise/spikes (<= +0.089), or moving the traced arcs within their stated uncertainty (+-0.023).
fix: Do not set an acceptance threshold on referent_gain this round, and do not let any owner report a delta in it as progress. Use it exactly as the report's own section 4 recommends - alongside its controls - and treat 'is it above the smooth-shape ceiling at this mask_px' as the only readable question.

Replace the fixed ellipse_1.35 control with a real null: sweep aspect 1.0-2.0 in 0.05 steps and print the MAX, and add the 4-parameter superellipse/egg family maximum. On the SUITE frame that changes the printed null from +0.026 to +0.43. Any headline must then be quoted as (gain - smooth_ceiling), which for the shipped fruit today is NEGATIVE: 0.300 - 0.434 = -0.134.

Report a self-consistency number with every run: rasterise the argmax referent twice at this mask_px and score it against itself. That prints the instrument's unit at this raster (0.71-0.98) so nobody reads 0.300 as '30% of the way to a real apple'.

Either drop kiwi_half from the max (it contributes the single highest smooth-shape score, +0.567, and the file's claim that it cannot be gamed is false) or weight each referent's gain by its own boundary RMS so a near-circular referent cannot win the max.

Fix tools/probes.py line 143: it says referent_gain is max_j limb_gain_j; the code computes max_j min(limb_gain_j, sig_gain_j). The paragraph arguing against a min contradicts the shipped implementation and would lead a reader to quote the field the author says is gameable.

The cheapest real improvement is more referents with LARGE boundary RMS. strawberry (0.137) resists the smooth attack four times better than kiwi (0.054): the smooth egg gets +0.195 on strawberry alone versus +0.567 on kiwi. A second sharp black-background plate, or the pineapple crown from a source where it is not clipped, would matter more than any change to the scoring formula.
